rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Forces split by their bookkeeping. **Conservative forces** — gravity, the spring, electrostatic — do work independent of path and zero work around any closed loop; their work can be stored as potential energy ($W = -\Delta PE$), and mechanical energy is conserved.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - W_conservative (closed path) = 0 - W_conservative = −(PE_f − PE_i) - With friction: KE₁ + PE₁ = KE₂ + PE₂ + E_heat

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Gravity vs friction receipts:** gravity returns exactly what it took (path-independent); friction keeps everything (path-dependent, dissipative).  ·  **Conservative ≠ 'always helpful':** gravity can do negative work on the way up — conservativeness is about bookkeeping, not direction.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Friction does NOT have a potential energy — the energy becomes heat, not stored PE.  ·  A conservative force does NOT guarantee energy conservation if non-conservative forces are also present.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Staircase vs lift*** — lifting a box by h costs mgh by either route; dragging it there on rough floor costs differently by each route.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: No verified PYQ in the bank; practise the two definitions with examples as NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Solve 5 problems classifying forces as conservative or non-conservative using the closed-loop test.  ·  Solve 5 mixed-system problems using W_nc = ΔE_mech.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (3m): Show that if a force's work depended on the path, energy could be created.** — Take two paths A and B between the same points with different works W_A > W_B. Go out by A and return by B: net work W_A − W_B > 0 on a closed loop, repeatable indefinitely — free energy from nowhere, violating conservation.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **PE exists only where work is path-independent:** the very definability of mgh rests on gravity's conservativeness.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Conservative: path-independent work, zero closed-loop work, PE definable, mechanical energy conserved — gravity, spring, electrostatic.  ·  Non-conservative: path-dependent, dissipative — friction, air resistance, viscosity.  ·  W_conservative = −ΔPE.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Perpetual-motion machines fail exactly here: any force returning a system to its start with net work gained would violate energy conservation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The closed-loop test is the definitive way to classify a force as conservative or not.  ·  Normal force is conservative (work = 0 when displacement is perpendicular).  ·  NEB frequently asks: 'Is this force conservative? Justify using the closed-loop test.'
